speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs. To understand the nature of this condition, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest, along with diplopia on looking up or down, strongly suggests a neuromuscular disorder. REQUEST TEST: Routine Blood Work (including Creatine Kinase, Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies, and Antinuclear Antibodies). REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG).

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor

That confirms the clinical picture of a neuromuscular junction disorder, specifically Myasthenia Gravis, as the antibody results and EMG findings are diagnostic.
